source_text: ὀφθαλμοὺς, τὸν ἥκιστα μὲν τοῦ βλέπειν ἐστερημένον, ὑγιῶς δὲ τοῦτο ποιεῖν οὐκ ἔχοντα. ὁποῖοί τινες εἶεν, οἷς ἔνεστι μὲν ἡ φρόνησις, τό γε μὴν ἑλέσθαι φρονεῖν ὀρθῶς οὐχ ὁρᾶται προσόν. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ὁρῶντες, φησὶ, τὸ ἀγαθὸν, ἐφ' ἂ μὴ προσῆκε τῶν ἰδίων θελημάτων παρατρέπουσι τὴν ῥοπήν· οἱ δὲ, καὶ δογματικῆς ὀρθότητος οὐκ ἀμοιρεῖν ἰσχύοντες, μονονουχὶ τὸν οἰκεῖον αὐτοὶ κατασίνονται νοῦν, εἰς ἀκαλλεστάτην ἐννοιῶν ἱέντες θήραν, καὶ ὑγιὲς οὐδὲν τῆς ἐπὶ Θεῷ δόξης εἰσδεχόμενοι· ὁποῖοί τινές εἰσιν, αἱρετικῶν μὲν μάλιστα παῖδες, Ἰουδαῖοί τε πρὸς τούτοις, οἱ Θεὸν μὲν πιστεύοντες εἶναι τὸν Πατέρα, τόν γε μὴν ἐξ αὐτοῦ πεφηνότα κατὰ φύσιν Υἱὸν ἀνοητότατα διωθούμενοι. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἀληθὲς ἐπ' αὐτοῖς τὸ διὰ τοῦ προφήτου φωνῆς ὑμνούμενον, «Ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῖς, καὶ οὐ βλέπουσιν.» Ὀνίνησι γὰρ τὸ βλέπειν οὐδὲν, εἰ μὴ προορῷτό τισι τὸ ὑγιῶς βλέπειν, καθάπερ ἀμέλει καὶ τὴν χωλότητα, καὶ τὸ σύντριμμα τοῦ ποδὸς ἐν ἴσῳ τετάχθαι λόγῳ δικαίως ἐλέγομεν· διοίσει γὰρ ὅλως οὐδὲν, τοῦ μηδ' ὅλως ἰέναι δύνασθαι, τὸ μὴ ὑγιῶς ἰέναι τυχὸν, τὴν ὡς ἐν πράγμασι δὲ δηλονότι τρίβον, καὶ τὴν ὡς ἐν ἔργοις ὁδόν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ λέγεις. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐ προσελεύσεται δὲ ἱερουργήσων ἄνθρωπος, ᾧ ἐὰν ᾖ ἐπ' αὐτῷ ψώρα ἀγρία, ἢ λειχὴν, ἢ μόνορχις, ἢ πᾶς ᾧ ἐστιν ἐν αὐτῷ μῶμος. Ψώρᾳ μὲν οὖν ἀγρίᾳ παρεικαστέον τὰ ἐκτοπώτατα τῶν παθῶν, δριμυτέροις ῥεύμασι καταχεόμενα νοῦ, καὶ πέρα παντὸς ἰόντα μέτρου, καὶ ἐξ ἡδονῆς μὲν ἔχοντα τὴν ἀρχὴν, εἰς πικρόν γε μὴν ἐξήκοντα τέλος. Ἢ οὐχὶ δὴ φὴς ἑκάστῳ τῶν πλημμελημάτων καὶ συμμετρίαν τινὰ καὶ ἀμετρίαν ὁρᾶσθαι τοῦ κακοῦ; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς ἔφης; {ΚΥΡ.} Ὁ σωματικῆς ἡδονῆς ἡττώμενος, οὐκ ἂν τοῦτο πάθοι καὶ μετρίως καὶ ὑπὲρ μέτρον; Οἱ μὲν γὰρ, ἥττηνται μόνον, καὶ νοσοῦσι περιεσταλμένως· οἱ δὲ καὶ εἰς ἄκρον ἥκουσι τοῦ κακοῦ, καὶ ἀσχέτως ἀγριαίνουσαν νοσοῦσι τὴν ἡδονὴν, ὡς καὶ αὐτῶν ἐπέκεινα τῶν κατὰ φύσιν ἐξολισθῆσαι παθῶν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Συνίημι ὃ φής. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν κακῶν τὸ ἐκτόπως ἐκνενευκὸς εἰς τὸ πέρα λόγου, καὶ μέτρων ἐπέκεινα τῶν ἐν ἔθει καὶ παρὰ πολλοῖς, λέγοιτ' ἂν ἡ ἀγρία ψώρα λοιπόν. Λειχὴν δὲ πρὸς τούτοις, πᾶν ὁτιοῦν πάθος, ἀεὶ διέρπον εἰς τὸ εὐρὺ, καὶ ἀκατάληκτον ἔχον τὴν εἰς τὸ χεῖρον ἐπίδοσιν. Συστέλλεσθαι δὲ δεῖν, καὶ εἰς τὸ μεῖον ἄγεσθαι πρὸς ἡμῶν τὰ προσπίπτοντα τῶν παθῶν, ὁ θεῖος βούλεται νόμος. Τοιοῦτόν τι νοήσεις ἀκούων· «Ἐὰν Πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐξουσιάζοντος ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ σὲ, τόπον σου μὴ ἀφῇς, ὅτι ἴαμα καταπαύσει ἁμαρτίας μεγάλας.» Τὰ γὰρ ἀνεπίπληκτα τῶν παθῶν, ἕρπει μὲν ἀεὶ πρὸς τὸ αἰσχιόνως ἔχον· καταδράττεται δὲ καρδίας καὶ νοῦ, καὶ εἰς ὄλεθρον ἄγει παντελῆ. Δεῖ δὴ οὖν ἄρα πρὸς ἡμῶν ἐπιτιμᾶσθαι τὸ φαῦλον, ταῖς εἰς τὸ ἄμεινον ἀναδρομαῖς περιστελ
pass_a_gloss: [the one with lashless] eyes: the one least deprived of seeing, but not able to do this soundly. Such would be those in whom understanding (φρόνησις) is present, yet the choosing to think rightly is not seen to be there. For some, he says, seeing the good, turn aside the inclination of their own wills to things that were not fitting; others, though able not to lack a share of doctrinal rightness, all but ravage their own mind themselves, launching into a most unlovely hunt of notions, and admitting nothing sound of the opinion about God. Such are above all the children of heretics, and the Jews besides, who believe the Father to be God, but most senselessly thrust away the Son who appeared from him by nature. Therefore true of them is what is sung through the prophet's voice: 'Eyes to them, and they do not see.' For seeing profits nothing, unless seeing soundly is provided for by them, just as indeed we rightly said that lameness and the crushing of the foot are ranked in equal account; for not to go soundly perhaps will differ not at all from not being able to go at all, meaning the path as in affairs and the road as in works. PALL.: You speak well. CYR.: There shall not come near to act as priest a man on whom there is a wild itch, or lichen, or one-testicled, or anyone in whom there is a blemish. To the wild itch then must be likened the most outlandish of the passions, poured down on the mind in sharper streams, and going beyond every measure, and having the beginning from pleasure, but coming out to a bitter end. Or do you not say that in each of the faults both a certain due measure and a lack of measure of the evil is seen? PALL.: How did you say? CYR.: The one worsted by bodily pleasure, would he not suffer this both moderately and beyond measure? For some are only worsted, and are sick in a restrained way; others even come to the peak of the evil, and are sick with pleasure raging unchecked, so as to slip beyond even the passions that are according to nature. PALL.: I understand what you say. CYR.: So in each of the evils, what has outlandishly swerved to beyond reason, and beyond the measures in custom and among the many, would then be called the wild itch. Lichen besides these: any passion whatever, always creeping through into breadth, and having unceasing advance to the worse. The divine law wills that the passions falling on us be contracted and brought to less by us. Some such thing you will understand on hearing: 'If a spirit of the one in power goes up against you, do not leave your place, because healing will stop great sins.' For the unrebuked of the passions creep always toward the more shameful state; they seize heart and mind and lead into complete ruin. So then the base must be rebuked by us, the sobriety in us by runnings back to the better wrapping it round
pass_b_english: Cyril: …eyes is the one who is by no means deprived of sight, yet cannot see soundly. Such would be those who have understanding, but in whom no choice to think rightly is seen. For some, he means, see what is good, yet turn the bent of their own wills aside toward what they ought not; others, though they could have a share in right doctrine, all but ruin their own minds themselves: they throw themselves into a most unlovely hunt after notions and accept nothing sound in their belief about God. Such above all are the children of the heretics, and the Jews besides, who believe that the Father is God, yet most foolishly thrust away the One who has come forth from him, the Son by nature. So the word proclaimed by the voice of the prophet is true of them: ‘They have eyes, and they do not see’ (Jeremiah 5:21). For seeing is of no use unless care is taken that one sees soundly, just as we rightly said that lameness and the crushed foot are placed on the same footing. For it will make no difference at all whether one cannot walk at all or perhaps does not walk soundly, meaning, of course, the path of conduct and the road of deeds.

Cyril: ‘No man shall come near to serve as priest who has a raging itch or a spreading rash on him, or who has only one testicle, or anyone who has any blemish in him’ (Leviticus 21:20–21). We should liken the raging itch to the most monstrous of the passions, which pour down on the mind in sharper, more acrid streams and pass all measure, and which begin in pleasure but end in bitterness. Or would you not say that in each kind of sin the evil is seen in a measured form and also beyond measure?

Cyril: The man overcome by bodily pleasure: could he not suffer this both moderately and beyond measure? Some are only overcome, and are sick in a restrained way; others reach the height of the evil and are sick with a pleasure that rages out of control, so that they slip even beyond the passions that belong to nature.
Palladius: I understand what you mean.

Cyril: So in each of the evils, whatever has strayed monstrously beyond reason, and beyond the measures that are usual and common among most people, may be called the raging itch. The spreading rash, besides, is any passion at all that keeps creeping outward over a wider area and never stops growing worse. But the divine law wants us to check the passions that befall us and to reduce them. You will understand something of this kind when you hear: ‘If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, do not leave your place, for healing will put an end to great sins’ (Ecclesiastes 10:4). For passions left unrebuked always creep toward a more shameful state; they seize heart and mind and lead to utter ruin. So we must rebuke what is base, while the sobriety within us, by turning back again toward what is better, keeps it

choices.why: Leviticus 21:20–21: ψώρα ἀγρία rendered 'raging itch' to keep Cyril's play with ἀγριαίνουσαν ('rages'); λειχήν rendered 'spreading rash' to match his gloss (διέρπον εἰς τὸ εὐρύ); μόνορχις 'only one testicle'.
Pass A sense kept in the reading text.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

'They have eyes, and they do not see' matches LXX Jeremiah 5:21 word for word (ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῖς καὶ οὐ βλέπουσιν), and 'through the voice of the prophet' fits Jeremiah; the verb ὑμνούμενον ('sung') could suggest the Psalms (Psalm 115:5 = LXX 113:13, 'ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ οὐκ ὄψονται'), but the wording points to Jeremiah. 'He means' renders an unclear φησί in 'Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ὁρῶντες, φησὶ'. 'Son by nature' keeps κατὰ φύσιν Υἱόν (Cyril's anti-Arian term). Leviticus 21:20–21: ψώρα ἀγρία rendered 'raging itch' to keep Cyril's play with ἀγριαίνουσαν ('rages'); λειχήν rendered 'spreading rash' to match his gloss (διέρπον εἰς τὸ εὐρύ); μόνορχις 'only one testicle'. 'The passions that belong to nature' (τῶν κατὰ φύσιν παθῶν) may hint at unnatural vice (cf. Romans 1:26–27) but no citation is given. Ecclesiastes 10:4 is cited verbatim from the LXX; 'the spirit of the ruler' is the ruler's anger, which Cyril applies to an assault of passion. The section ends inside a genitive absolute (περιστελ|λούσης); section 7 opens '…in check'.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): [πτιλὸν τοὺς] ὀφθαλμούς: τὸν ἥκιστα τοῦ βλέπειν ἐστερημένον 'least deprived of seeing', ὑγιῶς δὲ τοῦτο ποιεῖν οὐκ ἔχοντα 'not able to do it soundly'. Such: οἷς ἔνεστι ἡ φρόνησις (understanding), but τὸ ἑλέσθαι φρονεῖν ὀρθῶς 'choosing to think rightly' not seen. οἱ μὲν ὁρῶντες τὸ ἀγαθόν 'some seeing the good' παρατρέπουσι τὴν ῥοπήν (turn aside the inclination) of their own θελήματα (wills) to what is not fitting; οἱ δέ, able not to lack δογματικῆς ὀρθότητος (doctrinal correctness), μονονουχὶ κατασίνονται τὸν οἰκεῖον νοῦν 'all but ravage their own mind', ἱέντες εἰς ἀκαλλεστάτην ἐννοιῶν θήραν 'launching into a most unlovely hunt of notions', receiving nothing ὑγιὲς (sound) τῆς ἐπὶ Θεῷ δόξης (of the opinion/glory concerning God). Such: αἱρετικῶν παῖδες 'children of heretics', and Ἰουδαῖοι, believing the Father to be God, but τὸν ἐξ αὐτοῦ πεφηνότα κατὰ φύσιν Υἱόν 'the natural Son who appeared from him' ἀνοητότατα διωθούμενοι 'most senselessly thrusting away'. So true is τὸ διὰ τοῦ προφήτου φωνῆς ὑμνούμενον: ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῖς καὶ οὐ βλέπουσιν. ὀνίνησι 'benefits' τὸ βλέπειν nothing εἰ μὴ προορῷτο τὸ ὑγιῶς βλέπειν 'unless seeing soundly is provided for'; as χωλότης and σύντριμμα τοῦ ποδός were ἐν ἴσῳ λόγῳ; no difference between μηδ' ὅλως ἰέναι 'not going at all' and μὴ ὑγιῶς ἰέναι 'not going soundly', i.e., the τρίβος (path) in πράγματα and ὁδός (road) in ἔργα. PALL: εὖ λέγεις. CYR: [Lev 21:20-21] οὐ προσελεύσεται ἱερουργήσων ἄνθρωπος with ψώρα ἀγρία (wild/raging itch-scab), λειχήν (lichen, spreading rash), μόνορχις (one-testicled), or anyone with μῶμος (blemish). ψώρα ἀγρία παρεικαστέον 'to be likened' to τὰ ἐκτοπώτατα τῶν παθῶν 'most outlandish passions', δριμυτέροις ῥεύμασι καταχεόμενα νοῦ 'pouring over the mind with sharper flows', πέρα παντὸς μέτρου, ἐξ ἡδονῆς ἀρχή, εἰς πικρὸν τέλος. Or in each πλημμέλημα (offence) is seen συμμετρία (measure) and ἀμετρία (measurelessness) τοῦ κακοῦ? PALL: πῶς ἔφης. CYR: the one ἡττώμενος (overcome) by σωματικὴ ἡδονή may suffer καὶ μετρίως καὶ ὑπὲρ μέτρον. some ἥττηνται μόνον, νοσοῦσι περιεσταλμένως 'sick in restrained way'; others εἰς ἄκρον ἥκουσι τοῦ κακοῦ, ἀσχέτως ἀγριαίνουσαν νοσοῦσι τὴν ἡδονήν 'sick with pleasure raging unchecked', ἐπέκεινα τῶν κατὰ φύσιν ... παθῶν ἐξολισθῆσαι 'slip beyond natural passions'. PALL: συνίημι. CYR: in each evil τὸ ἐκτόπως ἐκνενευκὸς εἰς τὸ πέρα λόγου 'what has swerved outlandishly beyond reason' and beyond μέτρα τῶν ἐν ἔθει καὶ παρὰ πολλοῖς 'customary measures among the many' = ἡ ἀγρία ψώρα. λειχήν = any πάθος ἀεὶ διέρπον εἰς τὸ εὐρύ 'always creeping out wide', ἀκατάληκτον ... τὴν εἰς τὸ χεῖρον ἐπίδοσιν 'ceaseless growth to worse'. ὁ θεῖος νόμος wills συστέλλεσθαι 'be contracted' and εἰς τὸ μεῖον ἄγεσθαι 'brought to less' the passions befalling. Quote ἐὰν πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐξουσιάζοντος ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ σέ, τόπον σου μὴ ἀφῇς, ὅτι ἴαμα καταπαύσει ἁμαρτίας μεγάλας. τὰ ἀνεπίπληκτα 'unrebuked' passions ἕρπει (creep) to the more shameful, καταδράττεται (grasp) heart and mind, lead εἰς ὄλεθρον παντελῆ. δεῖ ἐπιτιμᾶσθαι 'be rebuked' τὸ φαῦλον, ταῖς εἰς τὸ ἄμεινον ἀναδρομαῖς 'by runnings-back to the better', περιστελ[λούσης αὐτὸ τῆς ἐν ἡμῖν νήψεως ... in 7].

changes: sense fix: τῆς ἐπὶ Θεῷ δόξης is belief about God (the heretics' doctrine), not 'the glory due to God'
agency fix: εἰ μὴ προορῷτό τισι is passive ('unless care is taken that one sees soundly'), not 'one takes care first'
ῥοπή 'weight' calque -> 'the bent of their own wills', with παρατρέπουσι 'turn aside'
ἀκαλλεστάτην kept as superlative ('a most unlovely hunt'); δριμυτέροις kept comparative ('sharper, more acrid streams')
ἀναδρομαῖς: removed added 'our'; the sobriety itself turns back toward the better
Leviticus 21:20 order smoothed ('who has a raging itch or a spreading rash on him, or who has only one testicle')
checked: Jeremiah 5:21 LXX verbatim (Psalm 115:5 and Ezekiel 12:2 less close); Leviticus 21:20-21 (Cyril's paraphrase also draws on 21:18); Ecclesiastes 10:4 LXX verbatim
